answer.generated: Pooling achieves invariance to translation by reducing the spatial dimensions of the input while retaining important features through operations such as max-pooling, which selects the maximum value within a local neighborhood. This process inherently reduces the sensitivity to small translations since the selection of the maximum value across a localized area ensures that only the most prominent features survive, regardless of slight shifts in the input. In contrast, directly translating the input image would move the entire feature representation, leading to changes in the output that do not capture the essence of the feature itself but rather its position within the image.
